The code comment at line 225 says it must 'match the character before simplification normalizes its natural-number coefficient', so the author knows the LHS is not normal. findings.fix: Introduce a named character `negativeNonsimpleShortRootCharacter (k : Fin 2)` with `@[simp]` evaluation lemmas at `0` and `1` giving `-(α₀ + α₁)` and `-(2 • α₀ + α₁)`, and state both theorems in terms of it. Otherwise give two separately stated lemmas in normal form. Drop `@[simp↓]` from the eq_span theorem unless its LHS is simp-normal, matching the sibling `adjointWeightSpace_simpleRootCharacter_eq_span` (Space.lean:505), which has no simp attribute.
findings.issue: `adjointWeightSpace_negativeNonsimpleShortRoot_eq_span` (and `negativeNonsimpleShortRoot_mem_nontrivialAdjointWeights`, line 250) state the characters as `Multiplicative.ofAdd (-((k.val + 1) • simpleRootCharacter 0 + simpleRootCharacter 1))`. Consumers state these roots as `-(α₀ + α₁)` and `-(2 • α₀ + α₁)`, so after normalization or at concrete `k` the `@[simp↓]` LHS (`(↑(1 : Fin 2) + 1) • …`) never matches. Each use then needs a manual rewrite into the artificial form.

summary: The public surface encodes the two negative short-root characters as the non-normal form `-((k.val + 1) • α₀ + α₁)` behind a `Fin 2` index, and its `@[simp↓]` main theorem matches only that artificial form. The PR also proves a general weight-character injectivity fact again as a local helper instead of exporting it from its canonical home.
